name: Payoff Review
description: Case-pool variant of Return on Investment, for Problem Recognition.
formula: ROI = (Gain from Investment − Cost of Investment) / Cost of Investment × 100
business_contexts: a manufacturer weighing whether a new packaging line was worth the money it cost
a marketing team assessing whether a completed campaign was worth its spend
a retailer assessing whether a store remodel was worth its cost
a logistics company assessing whether a new routing system was worth its cost
a hospital assessing whether new equipment was worth its purchase price
question_patterns: Relative to what it cost, how much did the client actually get back from this investment?
Expressed as a percentage of what was spent, how well did this investment pay off?
How much value did this investment generate, relative to what it cost to make?
As a percentage of the original outlay, what did the client gain from this investment?
solution_logic: Step 1: Calculate net gain = gain_from_investment − cost_of_investment
Step 2: Calculate ROI = net gain / cost_of_investment × 100
key_insight: ROI measures net gain relative to what was put in — a positive ROI means the investment returned more than it cost, and a negative one means it didn't.
common_mistakes: Dividing by the gain instead of the cost of investment
Forgetting to subtract the cost of investment before dividing, which reports gross return instead of net
framework_soundbite: ROI is net gain over cost, times 100 — what you got back beyond what you put in, as a percentage.
